notas: A small brown string is tied around the cord after knot #6 in the second group (counting from the top).
The subsidiary of pendant #22 has been stitched to the pendant with modern thread.  It is not clear if the subsidiary truly belongs on this pendant or where its position should be.

Pendants 1-24 were mounted on cloth and stitched the opposite way from which most of the bundles fall.  There is no evidence that these were meant to be top cords.  Attachments have been read the reverse of what is visible, as they would appear if they were hanging in the same direction as the rest of the pendants.
Pendant #33 is knotted in a loop like a noose between 16.5 and 17.5 cm.
Pendant #69 was found in the bundle of pendants 63-70, but it was not attached to the primary cord.  Its location is uncertain.
The knot on this khipu is partly untied.
Pendant #88 has been patched in two places, 5.5 cm and 18.0 cm.  It is recorded as if it is a valid pendant, but its legitimacy is dubious.
Subsidiary #163s8 has been stitched onto its pendant cord, and it is not clear that this was its original position.
Pendants #292, #293, #294, and #295 are fragile and disintegrating.  Measurements taken from partial strings stitched to back.
